    "replaceAll":false,
    "originalFile":"# 217 — Variadic ports and the language-spec variadic shape\n\n## Status\nopen — Part A and Part B mechanics are in the codebase; Part C is\nthe active design question\n\n## What this issue is now\n\nThe original issue was titled \"Concat box with per-input variadic\nports and auto-grow/shrink.\" That framing has aged out:\n\n- There is no dedicated **concat box kind**. `M.concat(sep, ...)`\n  lives in `libs/text.lua` and is invoked by any call box that\n  imports it. The variadic UI work was never specific to concat.\n- The original \"split returns a JSON-encoded array on the single\n  output wire\" story was a phase-2 transport assumption. Phase 3\n  (issue 312, same-language wire fast path) classifies each edge\n  and only JSON-encodes when crossing a language boundary. So\n  `M.split` returning a Lua array is correct in-language and the\n  runtime bridges if the downstream box is a different language.\n\nThe issue is now about the **editor's variadic-port mechanic** and\nhow it interacts with the **language spec** — specifically, what\nthe editor's `var` toggle means and what governs whether it's\noffered.\n\n## Part A — `libs/text.lua` *(shipped)*\n\n`libs/text.lua` ships `M.concat(sep, ...)`, `M.split(text, sep)`,\nand (via issue 237) `upper`, `lower`, `trim`, `replace`,\n`replace_first`, `contains`, `starts_with`, `ends_with`, `length`,\n`substring`. All are pure string operations consumed by call\nboxes; no special box kind exists.\n\n`M.split` is most useful paired with the iterator box (issue 221)\nso each part fans out to its own dispatch. Without the iterator\nit's just \"an array on a wire\" — legitimate but flat.\n\n## Part B — Editor variadic data model *(shipped)*\n\nA box JSON can carry a `variadic_inputs` array of base names; slots\nare stored as `<base>_<index>` in the `inputs` array. The inspector\n(`assets/js/004-inspector.js`) implements:\n\n- `make_variadic(port_name)` — turn a plain port into a one-slot\n  variadic group (`text` → `text_0`).\n- `unmake_variadic(base)` — collapse back to a single port.\n- `add_variadic_slot(base)` — append `<base>_<last+1>` (auto-grow).\n- `remove_variadic_slot(slot_name)` — delete and renumber.\n- `auto_grow_after_set(box, slot_name)` — append a new empty slot\n  when the user uses the current last slot.\n\nAuto-grow triggers on wire-connect and on value-set. Shrinking is\nexplicit-only — `×` button per slot. Wire-disconnect and value-\nclear do **not** shrink, deliberately, so transient editing\ndoesn't lose structure.\n\nThe schema (`src/001-schema.lua`) accepts `variadic_inputs` as an\noptional array of strings.\n\n## Part C — What `var` actually means *(active design)*\n\n### Wrong model (rejected)\n\nThe earlier framing said: regex-parse each source file in the\neditor, mark functions whose signatures end in `...` / `\"$@\"` /\n`va_list` as \"variadic-capable,\" and gate the `var` toggle on\nthat per-function flag.\n\nThat model collapses on contact with the project's vision:\n\n1. **It's not a per-function fact.** Every Lua function accepts N\n   positional args. `function f(a)` called with five args silently\n   keeps the first; `...` in the signature is the *author's choice\n   to capture extras*, not a runtime constraint. Bash is the same\n   — every function gets `\"$@\"` whether it touches it or not. C\n   through the dispatch wrapper (issue 304) is the same —\n   `argc`/`argv` is the universal call shape.\n2. **It centralises language knowledge in the editor.** Per-\n   language regex parsers in the editor are exactly the\n   ossification the `langs/<name>/` model exists to prevent.\n   Adding a new language would mean writing a new regex.\n3. **It locks the editor to a static source view.** A function the\n   user is in the middle of editing might briefly not have `...`\n   in the signature; the editor would flicker the toggle on/off.\n\n### Right model: variadic shape is a language fact\n\nThe language declares its calling-convention shape once, in\n`langs/<name>/spec.js`:\n\n```js\nexport const LANGUAGE_SPEC = {\n  name: 'lua',\n  file_ext: '.lua',\n  variadic_shape: 'positional',\n};\n```\n\n`variadic_shape: 'positional'` means the language accepts N\npositional args at call time, period. Every shipped language today\n(Lua, Bash, C) declares this. Future languages with different\nshapes (Python `**kwargs`, streaming generators, tagged unions)\ndeclare their own shape — the editor's variadic UI eventually\ngrows variants for them, but `positional` covers everything we\nship.\n\nA language that genuinely cannot accept variadic input declares\n`variadic_shape: 'none'`, and the editor disables the `var` toggle\nfor all its boxes. We don't have one of those today.\n\n### Editor behaviour under this model\n\n- The `var` toggle on a port is gated by **language**, not by\n  function. For every Lua / Bash / C box today, the toggle is\n  available.\n- The user is responsible for matching wired arity to the\n  function's intent. The editor surfaces what the source declares\n  (via `parser.js`'s named parameters) so the user can see the\n  arity the author wrote. If they wire five inputs to a function\n  whose body only reads the first, that's a user choice — same\n  class as wiring a string into a port the function treats as a\n  number. The runtime doesn't police it.\n- Compile-time (issue 309) and validator (issue 002) checks\n  surface obvious mismatches as documentation, not as gates.\n\n### What `parser.js` does and doesn't do\n\n`langs/<name>/parser.js` continues to enumerate functions in a\nsource file and extract named parameter and return names. That\nfeeds the file browser. It does **not** compute any per-function\nvariadic property — the early `variadic_tail` field was removed\nin this issue's pass.\n\n### Implementation status\n\n- `langs/lua/spec.js`, `langs/bash/spec.js`, `langs/c/spec.js` —\n  shipped. Each exports `LANGUAGE_SPEC` with `variadic_shape:\n  'positional'`.\n- `langs/lua/parser.js`, `langs/bash/parser.js` — shipped without\n  `variadic_tail`. Still produce inputs/outputs for the file\n  browser.\n- `tests/234-language-spec-js-test.mjs` — shipped. Asserts every\n  spec.js exports a valid `LANGUAGE_SPEC` with a known\n  `variadic_shape`.\n- Inspector consumption of `LANGUAGE_SPEC.variadic_shape` —\n  **not yet wired**. Today the `var` toggle is offered\n  unconditionally; the gate-by-language step is the remaining\n  work.\n\n### Remaining work\n\n1. `assets/js/004-inspector.js::mk_port_display` — load the active\n   box's language spec (the same dynamic-import pattern used for\n   lexers), and hide the `var` button when\n   `variadic_shape !== 'positional'`. Today every shipped language\n   is positional, so this is a future-proofing step rather than a\n   visible change.\n2. Inspector renders the parsed signature near the box header so\n   the user always sees the function's declared arity. This is the\n   documentation half of the design — replaces the rejected \"gate\n   the toggle per function\" approach with \"show the arity, let the\n   user judge.\"\n3. Update `docs/005-language-specs.md` with a \"language spec for\n   the editor\" section pointing at `spec.js` as the canonical\n   home for editor-facing language facts (variadic shape, future\n   additions).\n\n## Future development ideas\n\n### Variadic shapes that aren't `positional`\n\n- `keyed` — Python `**kwargs`, Ruby keyword splats. Slot model is\n  `(key, value)` pairs, user labels per slot, not auto-numbered.\n- `tagged` — Rust enum lists, Haskell heterogeneous lists. Per-\n  slot `(tag, value)`.\n- `stream` — generators, channels, iterators. One slot, queued.\n  Closer to issue 213's queued-input model than to positional\n  variadic.\n\nEach shape has its own auto-grow rule and inspector controls. The\nlanguage spec declares which shape applies; the editor renders\naccordingly. None of these are shipped — the positional shape\ncovers every language so far. Captured here so the design door\nstays open.\n\n### Outputs\n\nThe single-output rule (issue 218) is unchanged. Variadic is an\ninput-side concern.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `libs/text.lua` — Part A library functions\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — Part B variadic mechanics, future\n  home for the spec-driven `var` gate\n- `src/001-schema.lua` — accepts `variadic_inputs`\n- `langs/lua/spec.js`, `langs/bash/spec.js`, `langs/c/spec.js` —\n  the language-level `variadic_shape` declarations\n- `langs/lua/parser.js`, `langs/bash/parser.js` — function\n  enumeration (no per-function variadic detection)\n- `tests/234-language-spec-js-test.mjs` — spec.js contract tests\n- `issues/231-move-signature-parsers-into-langs.md` — moved\n  signature parsing into `langs/<name>/parser.js`\n- `issues/312-same-language-wire-fast-path.md` — supersedes the\n  old \"JSON-encode every wire\" story Part A was framed against\n- `issues/221-iterator-box.md` — the canonical companion to\n  `M.split` for fan-out\n",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/217-variadic-ports-and-language-spec-shape.md"
  },

tracks gaps) | ongoing |\n| 233  | unified routing schema (comparator+iterator)    | open     |\n| 234  | middle-click duplicates the selected box        | complete |\n| 235  | literal value replaces port name on the canvas  | complete |\n| 236  | box header = filename, output label = `fn()`    | complete |\n| 237  | string-manipulation library expansion           | complete |\n| 238  | editor HTTP server config file                  | complete |\n| 216  | read-file box                                  | complete |\n| 217  | variadic ports and the language-spec variadic shape | A+B mechanics in; runtime in phase 3 / issue 304)\n- [x] Compile button (issue 222) — placeholder UI for the phase 3 build\n\n## Notes on graph model changes during phase 2\n\nThese are not new features so much as model corrections that shape\nwhat phase 3 will consume:\n\n- **Single-output rule** (218, complete): every box has exactly one\n  output wire. ## [422]

```json
{
  "userType":"external",
  "parentUuid":"91e9081f-50ca-4e0d-be4e-df1ff953fda6",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-20T20:27:53.761Z",
  "isSidechain":false,
  "cwd":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech",
  "sessionId":"eca8747e-4b7c-48e6-abc6-4daf904fec3f",
  "message":{
    "content":[{
        "name":"Bash",
        "id":"toolu_01E1QqPeTCotTBfyJdWZbDeG",
        "caller":{
          "type":"direct"
        },
        "type":"tool_use",
        "input":{
          "command":"git commit -m \"$(cat <<'EOF'\n217 — variadic toggle gates on the language, not on the function\n\nThe earlier model said: regex-parse each source file in the\neditor, look for `...` / `\"$@\"` / `va_list` in signatures, and\ngate the var toggle per function. That model collapses on contact\nwith the vision: every shipped language already accepts N\npositional args at call time. Variadic capability is a language\nfact, not a function fact, and centralising per-language regex\nparsing in the editor is exactly the ossification the langs/<name>/\ndirectory exists to prevent.\n\nThe right model is in langs/<name>/spec.js — each language\ndeclares its own variadic_shape, and the editor reads that one\nconstant. Today every language declares 'positional' so nothing\nchanges on screen; tomorrow a language that genuinely can't take\nvariadic input declares 'none' and its boxes lose the toggle\nautomatically.\n\nThe inspector grows a small spec registry (mirroring the lexer\nand parser registries already there), loads spec.js on demand\nwhen a box is selected, and consults the cached variadic_shape\nwhen painting the var button. Already-variadic groups keep their\ncollapse and remove controls regardless, so a future language\nflip can't trap an existing group.\n\nThe \"signature near the box header\" rendering that 217 also\nasked for already exists via issue 236 (header = filename, output\nport labeled with the function name), so no new rendering ships\nhere. The docs/005-language-specs.md section is deferred to the\nlanguage-spec contract work that's still being designed.\n\nTested via the existing JS test suite and a green make test (38\nunit-test binaries + 11 integration fixtures). The browser-side\nvisible behavior is unchanged today, which is the point.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",
          "description":"Commit 217 trinity"
        }

## [456]

```json
{
  "userType":"external",
  "parentUuid":"a138f558-b1e2-49fb-9556-a26513314b20",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-20T20:55:58.299Z",
  "isSidechain":false,
  "cwd":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech",
  "toolUseResult":{
    "stderr":"",
    "interrupted":false,
    "isImage":false,
    "noOutputExpected":false,
    "stdout":"commit efeb79b71435fe284a414fce92361361eadede0a\nAuthor: gabrilend <gabrilend@gmail.com>\nDate:   Tue May 19 21:35:35 2026 -0700\n\n    229 — read and write box kinds, with the editor surface to match\n    \n    The old data / file_write kinds always wore the wrong names. A box\n    named \"data\" doesn't say what it does; a sink named \"file_write\"\n    hides that it's a sink in a noun. Rename to verbs — read and write —\n    and reshape both to fit the data they actually move.\n    \n    A read box now emits a value. Sometimes that value lives in a file\n    and you give the box a path; sometimes the value is a small literal\n    you type in the inspector. Setting an inline value hides the path\n    port on the canvas — the box that has no file no longer pretends to\n    have one.\n    \n    A write box no longer disappears the moment it commits to disk. It\n    emits the boolean true downstream, so graphs that want to chain on\n    \"and now the file exists\" can fire whatever comes next; graphs that\n    don't care drop the boolean per the unwired-output rule. The same\n    rule already held informally everywhere; making it visible at the\n    sink puts it in writing.\n    \n    The editor's kind dropdown, the box colours, the header labels, the\n    inspector layout, and the architecture doc all line up behind the\n    new names. One end-to-end fixture exercises the inline-literal\n    path. The cross-language slice — where a Lua table reaches a C\n    struct natively across the wire — remains a documented next step,\n    because the bridges from 317 and the slot store don't yet share a\n    shape.       "content":"    ctx.lineWidth   = selected ? 2 : 1;\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, h, 6);\n    ctx.fill();\n    ctx.stroke();\n\n    ctx.shadowBlur = 0;\n\n    // header bar\n    ctx.fillStyle = color + '33';\n    ctx.beginPath();\n    ctx.roundRect(x, y, w, BOX_HEADER, [6, 6, 0, 0]);\n    ctx.fill();\n\n    // label — user override wins; otherwise the kind-driven default\n    // (issue 236): basename of ref for call boxes, plain kind name\n    // for everything else.\n    ctx.fillStyle  = '#e8eaf6';\n    ctx.font       = 'bold 12px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n    ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n    ctx.fillText(box.label || default_header(box), x + 10, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // kind badge (top right)\n    ctx.fillStyle  = color;\n    ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n    ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n    ctx.fillText(kind.toUpperCase(), x + w - 8, y + BOX_HEADER / 2);\n\n    // port dots and labels\n    const { inputs: in_pts, outputs: out_pts } = port_positions(box);\n\n    ctx.font      = '10px monospace';\n    ctx.fillStyle = '#9ea3c0';\n\n    in_pts.forEach((p, i) => {\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = '#2d3250';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = '#6c72a0';\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      // Label rendered into the canvas (issue 224 reverted the DOM-\n      // overlay experiment — a click-capturing <input> next to the dot\n      // was capturing drag attempts). Editing still happens in the inspector.\n      // What text we draw depends on whether a literal value is set\n      // and whether a wire occupies the port (issue 235).\n      ctx.fillStyle  = '#9ea3c0';\n      ctx.font       = '10px monospace';\n      ctx.textAlign  = 'left';\n      ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n      ctx.fillText(port_label_text(box, box.inputs.find(q => q.name === p.name)),\n                   p.x + PORT_R + 4, p.y);\n    });\n\n    out_pts.forEach(p => {\n      // comparator branches use distinct colors; single output uses kind color\n      const dot_color = p.name ? (BRANCH_COLOR[p.name] || color) : color;\n      ctx.beginPath();\n      ctx.arc(p.x, p.y, PORT_R, 0, Math.PI * 2);\n      ctx.fillStyle   = dot_color + '44';\n      ctx.strokeStyle = dot_color;\n      ctx.lineWidth   = 1.5;\n      ctx.fill();\n      ctx.stroke();\n\n      // Output label rendered to the LEFT of the dot. Branch names\n      // ('lt'/'eq'/'gt') and iterator slot names come straight from\n      // p.name; a call box's single output gets `fn()` synthesized\n      // (issue 236) so the wire reads as the return value of\n      // calling the function.\n      const out_label = output_label_text(box, p);\n      if (out_label) {\n        ctx.fillStyle  = dot_color;\n        ctx.font       = '9px monospace';\n        ctx.textAlign  = 'right';\n        ctx.textBaseline = 'middle';\n        ctx.fillText(out_label, p.x - PORT_R - 4, p.y);\n      }\n    });\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ draw_all\n  function draw_all(ctx, selected_id) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      draw_box(ctx, boxes[id], id === selected_id);\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ hit_test_port\n  // Returns {box_id, port_name, side, x, y} for the port under world point (wx,wy), or null.\n  // For output dots: port_name is null (single wire) or 'lt'/'eq'/'gt' (comparator).\n  function hit_test_port(wx, wy) {\n    for (const id in boxes) {\n      const { inputs, outputs } = port_positions(boxes[id]);\n      for (const p of [...inputs, ...outputs]) {\n        const dx = wx - p.x, dy = wy - p.y;\n        if (dx*dx + dy*dy <= (PORT_R + 4) * (PORT_R + 4)) {\n          return { box_id: id, port_name: p.name, side: p.side, x: p.x, y: p.y };\n        }\n      }\n    }\n    return null;\n  }\n  // }}}",

```json
{
  "userType":"external",
  "parentUuid":"6b8b355d-c50b-4ee2-8fe8-59969ac87340",

  "toolUseResult":{
    "newString":"## Status\ncomplete (2026-05-20) — nodule rendering, gutter-side port name,\nand literal-bound hit-test exclusion all in `assets/js/002-boxes.js`.\nThe sever-on-connect guard in `assets/js/004-inspector.js` stays\nas a defensive fallback per the issue's plan.",
    "userModified":false,
    "oldString":"## Status\nopen",
    "structuredPatch":[{
        "oldStart":1,
        "oldLines":7,
        "newStart":1,
        "newLines":10,
        "lines":[" # 239 — Literal-bound input ports shrink to a nodule, port name moves to the left"," "," ## Status","-open","+complete (2026-05-20) — nodule rendering, gutter-side port name,","+and literal-bound hit-test exclusion all in `assets/js/002-boxes.js`.","+The sever-on-connect guard in `assets/js/004-inspector.js` stays","+as a defensive fallback per the issue's plan."," "," ## Current behavior"," "]
      }],
    "replaceAll":false,
    "originalFile":"# 239 — Literal-bound input ports shrink to a nodule, port name moves to the left\n\n## Status\nopen\n\n## Current behavior\n\nPer issue 235 (complete), an input port whose literal value is\nset renders with the value in place of the port name. The dot\non the box's left edge stays full-size, and the port name\ndisappears from the canvas — only the value is visible. The\ninspector still owns the name, and the dot still works as a\nwire-grab target even though wiring into a port with a literal\nvalue would severs that literal on connect.\n\nWhat the user reading the map can see at a glance:\n\n```\n●  \"hello world\"\n```\n\nThe port's variable name (`text`, `prompt`, whatever it is in\nthe underlying function signature) is invisible on the canvas.\nA reader has to open the inspector to recover the binding.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA port with a literal value rendered in three pieces, in three\npositions, in this order left-to-right:\n\n```\ntext   ·   \"hello world\"\n```\n\n- **Port name** (`text`) — moved to the LEFT of the box's edge,\n  in the gutter just outside the box body. This is the\n  variable's identity, and 235's value-takes-over rendering\n  hid it. Pulling it out to the left puts the name back in\n  plain sight WITHOUT giving up the value display.\n- **Nodule** — a smaller, denser dot sitting where the regular\n  port dot would. About half the radius of a wired port's dot.\n  Visual marker only — it advertises \"this port is bound\" the\n  same way the regular dot advertises \"this port can be wired.\"\n  Color match its kind, same as the regular dot, so the eye\n  reads it as a port without confusion.\n- **Literal value** (`\"hello world\"`) — to the RIGHT of the\n  nodule, same position the regular port name occupies on a\n  wired port. Truncation rules from 235 still apply (24-char\n  limit with ellipsis, tooltip for the full value).\n\nA wired port stays exactly as it is today — full-size dot,\nname to its right, no left-of-box-edge label.\n\n### Wire-connect targeting disabled\n\nA literal-bound port is no longer a valid drag-target for\nwires. `Boxes.hit_test_port` excludes literal-bound input ports\nfrom its hit search, so:\n\n- The cursor over a nodule does NOT highlight the port for a\n  wire-grab.\n- The user cannot start drawing a wire from / to a literal-bound\n  port. To rebind, they clear the literal value in the inspector\n  first; the port then renders as a wirable dot again.\n\nToday, dropping a wire onto a port with a literal value silently\nclears the literal (per the existing inspector code, line ~656\nin `004-inspector.js`). That behavior was a defensible\ncompromise pre-239 because the value was the only visible\nstate — losing it to a wire was reversible by re-typing.\nPost-239 the user is explicitly indicating \"this is bound, no\nwires,\" so we honor that instead of dropping a value on accident.\n\n### Why this is better than the 235-only rendering\n\n- The user reading a map sees BOTH the variable identity and\n  the bound value, on one line, without inspector lookup.\n- The nodule is unambiguously \"not a wire target,\" so the user\n  doesn't waste a drag attempt only to learn the literal was\n  silently cleared.\n- The left-of-edge name uses canvas gutter space that is\n  currently empty, so the box body's horizontal budget is\n  unaffected.\n\n### Edge cases\n\n- **Multiple ports with literals**: each gets its own left-of-\n  edge name. Boxes with several literal-bound ports show a\n  cleanly-stacked column of names in the gutter.\n- **Variadic slot with a literal**: same rule as any other\n  port. The variadic group's auto-grow / hide-empty-trailing\n  rules from issue 217 are unaffected.\n- **Port name long enough to collide with the left-of-edge\n  gutter of an adjacent box**: clip with ellipsis at the box's\n  max gutter width (TBD constant; ~12 monospace chars at\n  10px gives ~72 world-px gutter, which is fine for typical\n  identifiers). Tooltip on hover for the full name, same as\n  235's value tooltip.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `assets/js/002-boxes.js`:\n   - Add a `port_is_literal_bound(box, i)` helper. Returns true\n     when the port has a value AND no incoming wire. (The same\n     three-state check `port_label_text` already does — pull it\n     into a shared helper.)\n   - In `draw_box`'s input-port loop: when literal-bound, draw\n     the nodule (half-radius, same fill/stroke style as a normal\n     dot) instead of the full dot; render the port name to the\n     LEFT of the dot position (textAlign right, with the box's\n     world x as the right edge); the value label drawing\n     continues unchanged (235 path).\n   - `hit_test_port`: skip ports that are literal-bound on\n     inputs. The output side is unaffected (outputs don't carry\n     literal values).\n2. `assets/js/006-wires.js::create_connection`: the\n   sever-literal-on-connect path in 004-inspector.js becomes\n   unreachable because the literal port can't be a drag target.\n   It can stay as a defensive guard in case some other code\n   path forces a connection.\n3. Tests: extend the 235 case set with two new cases:\n   - \"wire attached, literal present\" → still renders as wired\n     (wire wins, no nodule).\n   - \"literal only\" → renders nodule + left-name + right-value.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Nodule radius**: half (3px world) is a starting guess. Visual\n  weight will tell us if it should be smaller; refine after\n  shipping. Constant in 002-boxes.js so it's a one-line change.\n- **Gutter clip width**: 12 chars at 10px is a guess. Could be\n  expressed as a fraction of `BOX_W` to scale if BOX_W ever\n  changes. Probably not worth parameterizing today.\n- **Inspector indication of \"this port is literal-bound\"**: the\n  inspector already shows the value field; that's the only\n  binding state. No additional UI needed there — the canvas is\n  the place where the visual rule applies.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — `draw_box` input-port path,\n  `hit_test_port`, helpers\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — sever-on-connect guard\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — sever-on-set guard (still\n  fires when the user sets a literal through the inspector\n  while a wire is attached; the wire-into-literal direction is\n  the one this issue closes off)\n- `issues/completed/235-literal-value-replaces-port-name-on-canvas.md`\n  — the predecessor; the value-on-canvas rule this issue\n  retains, the dot-stays-the-same-size rule this issue\n  supersedes\n",

    "originalFile":"# 239 — Literal-bound input ports shrink to a nodule, port name moves to the left\n\n## Status\ncomplete (2026-05-20) — nodule rendering, gutter-side port name,\nand literal-bound hit-test exclusion all in `assets/js/002-boxes.js`.\nThe sever-on-connect guard in `assets/js/004-inspector.js` stays\nas a defensive fallback per the issue's plan.\n\n## Current behavior\n\nPer issue 235 (complete), an input port whose literal value is\nset renders with the value in place of the port name. The dot\non the box's left edge stays full-size, and the port name\ndisappears from the canvas — only the value is visible. The\ninspector still owns the name, and the dot still works as a\nwire-grab target even though wiring into a port with a literal\nvalue would severs that literal on connect.\n\nWhat the user reading the map can see at a glance:\n\n```\n●  \"hello world\"\n```\n\nThe port's variable name (`text`, `prompt`, whatever it is in\nthe underlying function signature) is invisible on the canvas.\nA reader has to open the inspector to recover the binding.\n\n## Intended behavior\n\nA port with a literal value rendered in three pieces, in three\npositions, in this order left-to-right:\n\n```\ntext   ·   \"hello world\"\n```\n\n- **Port name** (`text`) — moved to the LEFT of the box's edge,\n  in the gutter just outside the box body. This is the\n  variable's identity, and 235's value-takes-over rendering\n  hid it. Pulling it out to the left puts the name back in\n  plain sight WITHOUT giving up the value display.\n- **Nodule** — a smaller, denser dot sitting where the regular\n  port dot would. About half the radius of a wired port's dot.\n  Visual marker only — it advertises \"this port is bound\" the\n  same way the regular dot advertises \"this port can be wired.\"\n  Color match its kind, same as the regular dot, so the eye\n  reads it as a port without confusion.\n- **Literal value** (`\"hello world\"`) — to the RIGHT of the\n  nodule, same position the regular port name occupies on a\n  wired port. Truncation rules from 235 still apply (24-char\n  limit with ellipsis, tooltip for the full value).\n\nA wired port stays exactly as it is today — full-size dot,\nname to its right, no left-of-box-edge label.\n\n### Wire-connect targeting disabled\n\nA literal-bound port is no longer a valid drag-target for\nwires. `Boxes.hit_test_port` excludes literal-bound input ports\nfrom its hit search, so:\n\n- The cursor over a nodule does NOT highlight the port for a\n  wire-grab.\n- The user cannot start drawing a wire from / to a literal-bound\n  port. To rebind, they clear the literal value in the inspector\n  first; the port then renders as a wirable dot again.\n\nToday, dropping a wire onto a port with a literal value silently\nclears the literal (per the existing inspector code, line ~656\nin `004-inspector.js`). That behavior was a defensible\ncompromise pre-239 because the value was the only visible\nstate — losing it to a wire was reversible by re-typing.\nPost-239 the user is explicitly indicating \"this is bound, no\nwires,\" so we honor that instead of dropping a value on accident.\n\n### Why this is better than the 235-only rendering\n\n- The user reading a map sees BOTH the variable identity and\n  the bound value, on one line, without inspector lookup.\n- The nodule is unambiguously \"not a wire target,\" so the user\n  doesn't waste a drag attempt only to learn the literal was\n  silently cleared.\n- The left-of-edge name uses canvas gutter space that is\n  currently empty, so the box body's horizontal budget is\n  unaffected.\n\n### Edge cases\n\n- **Multiple ports with literals**: each gets its own left-of-\n  edge name. Boxes with several literal-bound ports show a\n  cleanly-stacked column of names in the gutter.\n- **Variadic slot with a literal**: same rule as any other\n  port. The variadic group's auto-grow / hide-empty-trailing\n  rules from issue 217 are unaffected.\n- **Port name long enough to collide with the left-of-edge\n  gutter of an adjacent box**: clip with ellipsis at the box's\n  max gutter width (TBD constant; ~12 monospace chars at\n  10px gives ~72 world-px gutter, which is fine for typical\n  identifiers). Tooltip on hover for the full name, same as\n  235's value tooltip.\n\n## Suggested implementation steps\n\n1. `assets/js/002-boxes.js`:\n   - Add a `port_is_literal_bound(box, i)` helper. Returns true\n     when the port has a value AND no incoming wire. (The same\n     three-state check `port_label_text` already does — pull it\n     into a shared helper.)\n   - In `draw_box`'s input-port loop: when literal-bound, draw\n     the nodule (half-radius, same fill/stroke style as a normal\n     dot) instead of the full dot; render the port name to the\n     LEFT of the dot position (textAlign right, with the box's\n     world x as the right edge); the value label drawing\n     continues unchanged (235 path).\n   - `hit_test_port`: skip ports that are literal-bound on\n     inputs. The output side is unaffected (outputs don't carry\n     literal values).\n2. `assets/js/006-wires.js::create_connection`: the\n   sever-literal-on-connect path in 004-inspector.js becomes\n   unreachable because the literal port can't be a drag target.\n   It can stay as a defensive guard in case some other code\n   path forces a connection.\n3. Tests: extend the 235 case set with two new cases:\n   - \"wire attached, literal present\" → still renders as wired\n     (wire wins, no nodule).\n   - \"literal only\" → renders nodule + left-name + right-value.\n\n## Open questions\n\n- **Nodule radius**: half (3px world) is a starting guess. Visual\n  weight will tell us if it should be smaller; refine after\n  shipping. Constant in 002-boxes.js so it's a one-line change.\n- **Gutter clip width**: 12 chars at 10px is a guess. Could be\n  expressed as a fraction of `BOX_W` to scale if BOX_W ever\n  changes. Probably not worth parameterizing today.\n- **Inspector indication of \"this port is literal-bound\"**: the\n  inspector already shows the value field; that's the only\n  binding state. No additional UI needed there — the canvas is\n  the place where the visual rule applies.\n\n## Relevant files\n\n- `assets/js/002-boxes.js` — `draw_box` input-port path,\n  `hit_test_port`, helpers\n- `assets/js/006-wires.js` — sever-on-connect guard\n- `assets/js/004-inspector.js` — sever-on-set guard (still\n  fires when the user sets a literal through the inspector\n  while a wire is attached; the wire-into-literal direction is\n  the one this issue closes off)\n- `issues/completed/235-literal-value-replaces-port-name-on-canvas.md`\n  — the predecessor; the value-on-canvas rule this issue\n  retains, the dot-stays-the-same-size rule this issue\n  supersedes\n",
    "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/issues/239-literal-port-shrinks-to-nodule-with-name-on-left.md"
  },

A literal-bound\nport shrinks its dot to a half-radius nodule, and the port's name\nmoves into the gutter to the left of the box edge — name visible,\nvalue visible, on one canvas line. Plain wired-or-empty ports\nlook exactly as they did. The nodule is also excluded from wire\nhit-testing, so a drag can't accidentally clobber a binding the\nuser explicitly chose. To rebind, clear the literal in the\ninspector; the port returns to a full dot and becomes a wire\ntarget again.\n\nA handful of constants now name the visual rules — NODULE_R for\nhalf the dot, GUTTER_MAX_CHARS for the name clip in the gutter.\nThe inspector's sever-on-set guard stays as a defensive backstop\neven though the wire path that triggered it is now closed off.\n\nNo canvas-rendering tests exist for the editor yet (see issue\n232's coverage map) — syntax and the full pre-existing suite are\ngreen; visible behavior is only honestly verified by loading a\nbrowser, which I have not done in this session.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 4.7 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nEOF\n)\"",

      "content":"-- Schema definitions and validators for SoraMech map files.\n-- Validates box files, meta.json, and drivers.json against the spec\n-- in docs/001-architecture.md. Used by both the runner and the server\n-- before any file is written to disk.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\nlocal M = {}\n\n-- {{{ valid_kinds\n-- `call` runs a language function. `read` and `write` are dispatch-\n-- layer IO primitives (issue 229) — `read` emits an inline literal\n-- or file contents, `write` commits a `value` to disk and emits a\n-- boolean done signal.\nlocal valid_kinds = { call = true, read = true, write = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ valid_branches\n-- null/nil means no comparator (single wire); the three strings are comparator outputs.\nlocal valid_branches = { lt = true, eq = true, gt = true }\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ err\nlocal function err(errors, msg)\n    errors[#errors + 1] = msg\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_connection\nlocal function validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n    -- from_branch is nil (no comparator) or one of \"lt\"/\"eq\"/\"gt\"\n    if c.from_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'from_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.from_branch ~= nil and not valid_branches[c.from_branch] then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] 'from_branch' must be nil, 'lt', 'eq', or 'gt'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_box == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_box'\")\n    end\n    if c.to_input == nil then\n        err(errors, \"connection[\" .. i .. \"] missing 'to_input'\")\n    end\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_box\nfunction M.validate_box(box)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(box) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"box must be a table\" }\n    end\n\n    if box.id == nil or type(box.id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'id'\")\n    end\n    if box.label == nil or type(box.label) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"missing or non-string 'label'\")\n    end\n    if box.kind == nil or not valid_kinds[box.kind] then\n        err(errors, \"missing or invalid 'kind' (must be 'call', 'read', or 'write')\")\n    end\n\n    if box.kind == \"call\" then\n        -- iterator boxes (issue 221) are a pure routing primitive: input\n        -- copies straight to a chosen output, no language function is\n        -- invoked. Such a box has no ref/fn — only `iterator_outputs`,\n        -- an ordered list of output slot names. Otherwise ref is required.\n        local is_iterator = box.iterator_outputs ~= nil\n        if not is_iterator then\n            if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n                err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n            end\n        end\n        if box.iterator_outputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.iterator_outputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'iterator_outputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.iterator_outputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'iterator_outputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- variadic_inputs: optional list of base names; each name must\n        -- correspond to a series of inputs named \"<base>_<index>\" in\n        -- box.inputs (the editor maintains this; we only check the\n        -- shape here). See issue 217 part B.\n        if box.variadic_inputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.variadic_inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.variadic_inputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional; if present it must be a string parseable as number at runtime\n        if box.comparand ~= nil and type(box.comparand) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' must be a string\")\n        end\n        -- has_output: optional; absence means \"true\" (default behavior).\n        -- false marks a sink box whose function has no return values\n        -- (issue 226); the runtime treats such boxes as terminal and the\n        -- editor hides the output port and inspector output section.\n        if box.has_output ~= nil and type(box.has_output) ~= \"boolean\" then\n            err(errors, \"'has_output' must be a boolean\")\n        end\n        -- Per-port `optional` flag (issue 230). Absent means false: the\n        -- port is required and must be either wired or carry a literal\n        -- value. The wire/literal/optional triple-check happens at the\n        -- graph level (validate-map.lua and the editor's compile path),\n        -- not here — this only validates per-port shape.\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) == \"table\" then\n            for i, p in ipairs(box.inputs) do\n                if type(p) == \"table\" and p.optional ~= nil and type(p.optional) ~= \"boolean\" then\n                    err(errors, \"'inputs[\" .. i .. \"].optional' must be a boolean\")\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- read / write: dispatch-layer IO primitives (issue 229). Shape\n    -- check is intentionally permissive — the graph loader does the\n    -- \"has a value or a path\" semantic check.\n    if box.kind == \"read\" or box.kind == \"write\" then\n        if box.value ~= nil and type(box.value) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'value' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.path ~= nil and type(box.path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'path' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ check_input_bindings\n-- Graph-level check from issue 230: every input port on every box\n-- must be in one of three states by compile time —\n--   1. a wire is connected to it\n--   2. a literal `value` is set on it\n--   3. it carries `optional: true`\n-- Otherwise the box would silently receive a missing arg at runtime\n-- and the bug would only surface where the function happens to\n-- reference it. The check fails loud and points at the exact box +\n-- port instead.\n--\n-- `boxes` is a table mapping box-id → box record (the shape the\n-- editor cache and the phase 2 loader's graph use). Returns an\n-- array of error strings; empty array means OK.\nfunction M.check_input_bindings(boxes)\n    local errors = {}\n\n    -- precompute: for each (to_box, to_input) → true if a wire targets it.\n    -- Connections live on both endpoints (issue 228), so scanning every\n    -- box's connection list overcounts but doesn't miss anything.\n    local wired = {}\n    for _, box in pairs(boxes) do\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.to_box and c.to_input then\n                wired[c.to_box .. \"\\0\" .. c.to_input] = true\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- stable per-box iteration for predictable error ordering\n    local ids = {}\n    for id, _ in pairs(boxes) do ids[#ids + 1] = id end\n    table.sort(ids)\n\n    for _, id in ipairs(ids) do\n        local box = boxes[id]\n        for _, p in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n            local has_wire    = wired[id .. \"\\0\" .. p.name] == true\n            local has_literal = p.value ~= nil and p.value ~= \"\"\n            local is_optional = p.optional == true\n            if not (has_wire or has_literal or is_optional) then\n                err(errors, \"box '\" .. id .. \"': input '\" .. tostring(p.name) ..\n                    \"' has no wire, no literal, and is not optional\")\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"drivers.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    for ext, path in pairs(drivers) do\n        if type(ext) ~= \"string\" or ext:sub(1, 1) ~= \".\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",
      "numLines":253,
      "startLine":1,
      "totalLines":253,
      "filePath":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/src/001-schema.lua"
    }

No ref/fn — the box body\n  // is just the counter + slot list. Each slot has a user-renamable\n  // name; the slot name lands in a connection's `from_branch` field\n  // exactly like a comparator branch name.\n  //\n  // The inspector edits the slot list; the dispatch layer is what\n  // actually rotates between them at runtime.\n\n  function is_iterator(box) {\n    return Array.isArray(box && box.iterator_outputs);\n  }\n\n  // Toggle the box ON as an iterator. Ref/fn/comparand are mutually\n  // exclusive with iterator routing (a routing primitive has no\n  // function to invoke), so they are stripped. All outgoing wires are\n  // dropped because the output shape changes from a single dot (or\n  // lt/eq/gt) to N named slots — same shape-change-clears-wires rule\n  // as the variadic input toggle.\n  async function make_iterator() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n\n    await sever_output_wires();\n\n    delete current_box.ref;\n    delete current_box.fn;\n    delete current_box.comparand;\n    delete current_box.has_output;\n    current_box.iterator_outputs = ['output_0'];\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Toggle iterator OFF. Drop the iterator_outputs field; sever\n  // outgoing wires (their from_branch values referenced slot names\n  // that no longer exist). The user re-picks a function via the\n  // browse button to restore ref/fn.\n  async function unmake_iterator() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n\n    await sever_output_wires();\n    delete current_box.iterator_outputs;\n    // Restore an empty ref/fn so the schema (which requires ref on\n    // non-iterator call boxes) accepts the save. The user picks a\n    // function via the browse button to populate them.\n    if (current_box.ref === undefined) current_box.ref = '';\n    if (current_box.fn  === undefined) current_box.fn  = '';\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Append a new slot with a placeholder name (`output_N`). The user\n  // can rename it after — placeholder is just to avoid prompting on\n  // every grow. Mirrors the variadic auto-grow pattern.\n  async function add_iterator_slot() {\n    if (!current_box || !is_iterator(current_box)) return;\n    const slots = current_box.iterator_outputs;\n    let n = slots.length;\n    // pick the lowest free `output_N` so renaming + adding doesn't\n    // collide with an existing user-named slot\n    while (slots.includes('output_' + n)) n++;\n    slots.push('output_' + n);\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Remove the slot at index `idx`. Outgoing wires whose from_branch\n  // matched the removed slot get severed; remaining slots keep their\n  // names (no rename — slot names are user-defined and free-form, no\n  // need to compact like the variadic numeric indexes).\n  async function remove_iterator_slot(idx) {\n    if (!current_box || !is_iterator(current_box)) return;\n    const slots = current_box.iterator_outputs;\n    if (idx < 0 || idx >= slots.length) return;\n    // Removing the last remaining slot collapses the iterator entirely\n    // — the user shouldn't have to know there's a separate \"toggle off\"\n    // button when the visual outcome of \"× the last slot\" is the same.\n    if (slots.length <= 1) {\n      return unmake_iterator();\n    }\n    const removed = slots[idx];\n\n    // Sever every outgoing wire on this branch.\n    const my_id = current_box.id;\n    const dst_ids = new Set();\n    (current_box.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n      if (c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed) dst_ids.add(c.to_box);\n    });\n    current_box.connections = (current_box.connections || [])\n      .filter(c => !(c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed));\n    for (const dst_id of dst_ids) {\n      const dst = Boxes.boxes[dst_id];\n      if (!dst) continue;\n      dst.connections = (dst.connections || [])\n        .filter(c => !(c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed));\n      try { await API.put_box(dst_id, dst); }\n      catch (e) { console.error('failed to clean wires to ' + dst_id + ': ' + e.message); }\n    }",

Each slot has a user-renamable\n330\t  // name; the slot name lands in a connection's `from_branch` field\n331\t  // exactly like a comparator branch name.\n332\t  //\n333\t  // The inspector edits the slot list; the dispatch layer is what\n334\t  // actually rotates between them at runtime.\n335\t\n336\t  function is_iterator(box) {\n337\t    return Array.isArray(box && box.iterator_outputs);\n338\t  }\n339\t\n340\t  // Toggle the box ON as an iterator. Ref/fn/comparand are mutually\n341\t  // exclusive with iterator routing (a routing primitive has no\n342\t  // function to invoke), so they are stripped. All outgoing wires are\n343\t  // dropped because the output shape changes from a single dot (or\n344\t  // lt/eq/gt) to N named slots — same shape-change-clears-wires rule\n345\t  // as the variadic input toggle.\n346\t  async function make_iterator() {\n347\t    if (!current_box) return;\n348\t\n349\t    await sever_output_wires();\n350\t\n351\t    delete current_box.ref;\n352\t    delete current_box.fn;\n353\t    delete current_box.comparand;\n354\t    delete current_box.has_output;\n355\t    current_box.iterator_outputs = ['output_0'];\n356\t\n357\t    await save();\n358\t    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n359\t    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n360\t  }\n361\t\n362\t  // Toggle iterator OFF. Drop the iterator_outputs field; sever\n363\t  // outgoing wires (their from_branch values referenced slot names\n364\t  // that no longer exist). The user re-picks a function via the\n365\t  // browse button to restore ref/fn.\n366\t  async function unmake_iterator() {\n367\t    if (!current_box) return;\n368\t\n369\t    await sever_output_wires();\n370\t    delete current_box.iterator_outputs;\n371\t    // Restore an empty ref/fn so the schema (which requires ref on\n372\t    // non-iterator call boxes) accepts the save. The user picks a\n373\t    // function via the browse button to populate them.\n374\t    if (current_box.ref === undefined) current_box.ref = '';\n375\t    if (current_box.fn  === undefined) current_box.fn  = '';\n376\t\n377\t    await save();\n378\t    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n379\t    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n380\t  }\n381\t\n382\t  // Append a new slot with a placeholder name (`output_N`). The user\n383\t  // can rename it after — placeholder is just to avoid prompting on\n384\t  // every grow. Mirrors the variadic auto-grow pattern.\n385\t  async function add_iterator_slot() {\n386\t    if (!current_box || !is_iterator(current_box)) return;\n387\t    const slots = current_box.iterator_outputs;\n388\t    let n = slots.length;\n389\t    // pick the lowest free `output_N` so renaming + adding doesn't\n390\t    // collide with an existing user-named slot\n391\t    while (slots.includes('output_' + n)) n++;\n392\t    slots.push('output_' + n);\n393\t    await save();\n394\t    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n395\t    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n396\t  }\n397\t\n398\t  // Remove the slot at index `idx`. Outgoing wires whose from_branch\n399\t  // matched the removed slot get severed; remaining slots keep their\n400\t  // names (no rename — slot names are user-defined and free-form, no\n401\t  // need to compact like the variadic numeric indexes).\n402\t  async function remove_iterator_slot(idx) {\n403\t    if (!current_box || !is_iterator(current_box)) return;\n404\t    const slots = current_box.iterator_outputs;\n405\t    if (idx < 0 || idx >= slots.length) return;\n406\t    // Removing the last remaining slot collapses the iterator entirely\n407\t    // — the user shouldn't have to know there's a separate \"toggle off\"\n408\t    // button when the visual outcome of \"× the last slot\" is the same.\n409\t    if (slots.length <= 1) {\n410\t      return unmake_iterator();\n411\t    }\n412\t    const removed = slots[idx];\n413\t\n414\t    // Sever every outgoing wire on this branch.\n415\t    const my_id = current_box.id;\n416\t    const dst_ids = new Set();\n417\t    (current_box.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n418\t      if (c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed) dst_ids.add(c.to_box);\n419\t    });\n420\t    current_box.connections = (current_box.connections || [])\n421\t      .filter(c => !(c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed));\n422\t    for (const dst_id of dst_ids) {\n423\t      const dst = Boxes.boxes[dst_id];\n424\t      if (!dst) continue;\n425\t      dst.connections = (dst.connections || [])\n426\t        .filter(c => !(c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed));\n427\t      try { await API.put_box(dst_id, dst); }\n428\t      catch (e) { console.error('failed to clean wires to ' + dst_id + ': ' + e.message); }\n429\t    }"
      }],
    "role":"user"
  }
}

Otherwise ref is required.\n        local is_iterator = box.iterator_outputs ~= nil\n        if not is_iterator then\n            if box.ref == nil or type(box.ref) ~= \"string\" then\n                err(errors, \"box missing 'ref'\")\n            end\n        end\n        if box.iterator_outputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.iterator_outputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'iterator_outputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.iterator_outputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'iterator_outputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- fn is optional for binary callers (shell scripts, binaries)\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        -- variadic_inputs: optional list of base names; each name must\n        -- correspond to a series of inputs named \"<base>_<index>\" in\n        -- box.inputs (the editor maintains this; we only check the\n        -- shape here). See issue 217 part B.\n        if box.variadic_inputs ~= nil then\n            if type(box.variadic_inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n                err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs' must be an array\")\n            else\n                for i, name in ipairs(box.variadic_inputs) do\n                    if type(name) ~= \"string\" then\n                        err(errors, \"'variadic_inputs[\" .. i .. \"]' must be a string\")\n                    end\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        -- comparand: optional; if present it must be a string parseable as number at runtime\n        if box.comparand ~= nil and type(box.comparand) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'comparand' must be a string\")\n        end\n        -- has_output: optional; absence means \"true\" (default behavior).\n        -- false marks a sink box whose function has no return values\n        -- (issue 226); the runtime treats such boxes as terminal and the\n        -- editor hides the output port and inspector output section.\n        if box.has_output ~= nil and type(box.has_output) ~= \"boolean\" then\n            err(errors, \"'has_output' must be a boolean\")\n        end\n        -- Per-port `optional` flag (issue 230). Absent means false: the\n        -- port is required and must be either wired or carry a literal\n        -- value. The wire/literal/optional triple-check happens at the\n        -- graph level (validate-map.lua and the editor's compile path),\n        -- not here — this only validates per-port shape.\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) == \"table\" then\n            for i, p in ipairs(box.inputs) do\n                if type(p) == \"table\" and p.optional ~= nil and type(p.optional) ~= \"boolean\" then\n                    err(errors, \"'inputs[\" .. i .. \"].optional' must be a boolean\")\n                end\n            end\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    -- read / write: dispatch-layer IO primitives (issue 229). Shape\n    -- check is intentionally permissive — the graph loader does the\n    -- \"has a value or a path\" semantic check.\n    if box.kind == \"read\" or box.kind == \"write\" then\n        if box.value ~= nil and type(box.value) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'value' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.path ~= nil and type(box.path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"'path' must be a string\")\n        end\n        if box.inputs ~= nil and type(box.inputs) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'inputs' must be an array\")\n        end\n        if box.connections ~= nil then\n            for i, c in ipairs(box.connections) do\n                validate_connection(c, i, errors)\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    if box.ui ~= nil then\n        if type(box.ui) ~= \"table\" then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must be a table\")\n        elseif box.ui.x == nil or box.ui.y == nil then\n            err(errors, \"'ui' must have 'x' and 'y' fields\")\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ check_input_bindings\n-- Graph-level check from issue 230: every input port on every box\n-- must be in one of three states by compile time —\n--   1. a wire is connected to it\n--   2. a literal `value` is set on it\n--   3. it carries `optional: true`\n-- Otherwise the box would silently receive a missing arg at runtime\n-- and the bug would only surface where the function happens to\n-- reference it.  end\n\n    -- stable per-box iteration for predictable error ordering\n    local ids = {}\n    for id, _ in pairs(boxes) do ids[#ids + 1] = id end\n    table.sort(ids)\n\n    for _, id in ipairs(ids) do\n        local box = boxes[id]\n        for _, p in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n            local has_wire    = wired[id .. \"\\0\" .. p.name] == true\n            local has_literal = p.value ~= nil and p.value ~= \"\"\n            local is_optional = p.optional == true\n            if not (has_wire or has_literal or is_optional) then\n                err(errors, \"box '\" .. id .. \"': input '\" .. tostring(p.name) ..\n                    \"' has no wire, no literal, and is not optional\")\n            end\n        end\n    end\n\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_meta\nfunction M.validate_meta(meta)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(meta) ~= \"table\" then\n        return { \"meta.json must be a table\" }\n    end\n    if meta.name == nil or type(meta.name) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'name'\")\n    end\n    if meta.entry_box_id == nil or type(meta.entry_box_id) ~= \"string\" then\n        err(errors, \"meta.json missing 'entry_box_id'\")\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ validate_drivers\nfunction M.validate_drivers(drivers)\n    local errors = {}\n    if type(drivers) ~= err(errors, \"driver key '\" .. tostring(ext) .. \"' must be a dot-prefixed extension\")\n        end\n        if type(path) ~= \"string\" then\n            err(errors, \"driver value for '\" .. ext .. \"' must be a string path\")\n        end\n    end\n    return errors\nend\n-- }}}\n\nreturn M\n",

    "originalFile":"-- Synchronous FSM executor for the SoraMech runner.\n-- Walks the graph from the entry box, invokes language drivers for each\n-- box in dependency order, and threads output values through wires.\n-- Each box call is isolated in run_task() — the future thread pool swap point.\n\nlocal DIR = \"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech\"\n\npackage.path = DIR .. \"/libs/?.lua;\" ..\n               DIR .. \"/src/?.lua;\" ..\n               package.path\n\nlocal json = require(\"dkjson\")\nlocal M    = {}\n\n-- {{{ shell_quote\nlocal function shell_quote(s)\n    -- wrap a string in single quotes, escaping any embedded single quotes\n    return \"'\" .. tostring(s):gsub(\"'\", \"'\\\\''\") .. \"'\"\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ driver_path_for\nlocal function driver_path_for(ref, drivers)\n    -- binary callers (no extension mapping needed — they are executable directly)\n    -- source callers: look up extension in driver table\n    local ext = ref:match(\"%.([^./]+)$\")\n    if not ext then return ref end  -- no extension: treat as binary\n    local driver = drivers[\".\" .. ext]\n    return driver\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ run_task\n-- The task boundary. In v1: synchronous. Future: hand this signature to\n-- the thread pool. Returns a single output value and ok/err.\nlocal function run_task(box, inputs, drivers, map_dir)\n    local ref = box.ref\n    local fn  = box.fn\n\n    -- locate the driver for this ref\n    local driver = driver_path_for(ref, drivers)\n    if not driver then\n        return nil, \"no driver found for ref '\" .. ref .. \"'\"\n    end\n\n    -- resolve ref relative to map_dir\n    local abs_ref = map_dir .. \"/\" .. ref\n\n    -- build argument list: each input port's value as a JSON-encoded shell arg\n    local args = {}\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        local val = inputs[port.name]\n        if val == nil then\n            -- nil input becomes JSON null\n            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(nil))\n        else\n            args[#args + 1] = shell_quote(json.encode(val))\n        end\n    end\n\n    local cmd\n    if fn then\n        -- source caller: driver file fn arg_count [args...]\n        cmd = driver .. \" \" .. shell_quote(abs_ref) .. \" \" ..\n              shell_quote(fn) .. \" \" .. #args\n        for _, a in ipairs(args) do cmd = cmd .. \" \" .. a end\n    else\n        -- binary caller: run ref directly with args\n        cmd = abs_ref .. \" \" .. #args\n        for _, a in ipairs(args) do cmd = cmd .. \" \" .. a end\n    end\n\n    -- invoke driver; capture stdout; errors go to stderr (visible in terminal)\n    local tmpfile = map_dir .. \"/tmp/driver-stderr-\" .. box.id .. \".txt\"\n    local full_cmd = \"sh -c \" .. shell_quote(cmd .. \" 2>\" .. tmpfile)\n    local ph = io.popen(full_cmd, \"r\")\n    local stdout = ph:read(\"*a\")\n    local ok_close = ph:close()\n\n    -- read stderr if any\n    local sf = io.open(tmpfile, \"r\")\n    local stderr_text = sf and sf:read(\"*a\") or \"\"\n    if sf then sf:close() end\n    os.remove(tmpfile)\n\n    if not ok_close then\n        local err_msg = \"driver failed for box '\" .. box.id .. \"'\"\n        if stderr_text and #stderr_text > 0 then\n            err_msg = err_msg .. \": \" .. stderr_text:gsub(\"%s+$\", \"\")\n        end\n        return nil, err_msg\n    end\n\n    -- parse single JSON value from stdout; one output wire per box\n    local output_val, _, jerr = json.decode(stdout)\n    if jerr then\n        return nil, \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': driver stdout is not valid JSON: \" ..\n            tostring(jerr) .. \" (got: \" .. tostring(stdout):sub(1, 80) .. \")\"\n    end\n\n    return output_val, nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ inputs_satisfied\nlocal function inputs_satisfied(box, store)\n    -- a box is ready when all its declared input ports have a value in the store\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        if store[box.id .. \".\" .. port.name] == nil then\n            return false\n        end\n    end\n    return true\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ collect_inputs\nlocal function collect_inputs(box, store)\n    local inputs = {}\n    for _, port in ipairs(box.inputs or {}) do\n        inputs[port.name] = store[box.id .. \".\" .. port.name]\n    end\n    return inputs\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ fire_connections\n-- Routes the single output value through wired connections.\n-- If box.comparand is set: compare output against it (must be a number or error).\n-- Otherwise: fire all connections whose from_branch is nil.\n-- Returns nil on success, or an error string.\nlocal function fire_connections(box, output_val, store, queue, boxes)\n    if box.comparand and box.comparand ~= \"\" then\n        -- comparator mode: output must be a number\n        local comparand = tonumber(box.comparand)\n        if not comparand then\n            return \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': comparand '\" ..\n                tostring(box.comparand) .. \"' is not a valid number\"\n        end\n        local num_val = tonumber(output_val)\n        if not num_val then\n            return \"box '\" .. box.id .. \"': output value '\" ..\n                tostring(output_val) .. \"' is not a number, but comparator is configured\"\n        end\n\n        -- determine which branch to fire\n        local branch\n        if num_val < comparand then\n            branch = \"lt\"\n        elseif num_val == comparand then\n            branch = \"eq\"\n        else\n            branch = \"gt\"\n        end\n\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box ~= box.id then goto next_cmp_conn end\n            if c.from_branch == branch then\n                store[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = output_val\n                local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n                if target and inputs_satisfied(target, store) then\n                    queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box\n                end\n            end\n            ::next_cmp_conn::\n        end\n    else\n        -- single-wire mode: fire connections where from_branch is nil\n        for _, c in ipairs(box.connections or {}) do\n            if c.from_box ~= box.id then goto next_conn end\n            if c.from_branch == nil then\n                store[c.to_box .. \".\" .. c.to_input] = output_val\n                local target = boxes[c.to_box]\n                if target and inputs_satisfied(target, store) then\n                    queue[#queue + 1] = c.to_box\n                end\n            end\n            ::next_conn::\n        end\n    end\n    return nil\nend\n-- }}}\n\n-- {{{ write_last_run\nlocal function write_last_run(map_dir, run_state)\n    local tmp_dir = map_dir .. \"/tmp\"\n    local path    = tmp_dir .. \"/last-run.json\"\n    local f, ferr = io.open(path, \"w\")\n    if not f then\n        io.stderr:write(\"executor: cannot write last-run.json: \" .. tostring(ferr) .. \"\\n\")\n        return\n    end\n    f:write(json.encode(run_state, { local box = boxes[id]\n        if not box then\n            map_ok  = false\n            map_err = \"unknown box in queue: '\" .. id .. \"'\"\n            break\n        end\n\n        -- skip boxes whose inputs are not yet satisfied\n        if not inputs_satisfied(box, store) then\n            goto next_iter\n        end\n\n        if visited[id] then\n            goto next_iter\n        end\n inputs = inputs,\n            output = output_val,\n            status = task_err and \"error\" or \"ok\",\n            error  = task_err,\n        }\n\n        if task_err then\n            map_ok  = \" .. conn_err .. \"\\n\")\n            break\n        end\n\n        ::next_iter::\n    end\n\n    -- write last-run snapshot to tmp/\n    write_last_run(map_dir, {\n        ok    = map_ok,\n         "input":{
          "new_string":"  // {{{ Routing helpers (issue 233)\n  // Every call box carries a `routing` field declaring how its\n  // single output reaches downstream wires. Three kinds ship\n  // today (plain / comparator / iterator); randomizer / weighted\n  // / distributor / multi-band-comparator have their own follow-on\n  // issues (240–243).\n  //\n  // Plain is the default for a newly-created box. Switching kinds\n  // severs every outgoing wire because the output port shape\n  // changes — same shape-change-clears-wires rule the variadic\n  // input toggle uses.\n  //\n  // Iterator routing is a pure routing primitive: no language\n  // function is invoked, ref/fn are not set. Iterator port names\n  // are fixed as `out_0`, `out_1`, ... `out_<n-1>` (not user-\n  // renameable — the read-only-port-name rule from issue 224\n  // applies on the output side too).\n\n  // {{{ function routing_kind()\n  function routing_kind(box) {\n    return (box && box.routing && box.routing.kind) || 'plain';\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ function default_routing_for()\n  function default_routing_for(kind) {\n    if (kind === 'comparator') return { kind: 'comparator', comparand: 0 };\n    if (kind === 'iterator')   return { kind: 'iterator',   n_outputs: 2 };\n    return { kind: 'plain' };\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ async function set_routing_kind()\n  async function set_routing_kind(kind) {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n    if (routing_kind(current_box) === kind) return;\n    await sever_output_wires();\n    current_box.routing = default_routing_for(kind);\n    if (kind === 'iterator') {\n      // Iterator boxes are routing primitives — no function.\n      delete current_box.ref;\n      delete current_box.fn;\n      delete current_box.has_output;\n    } else {\n      // Plain/comparator need a function. Restore empty ref/fn\n      // so the schema (which requires ref on non-iterator call\n      // boxes) accepts the save; the user picks via the browse\n      // button to populate them.\n      if (current_box.ref === undefined) current_box.ref = '';\n      if (current_box.fn  === undefined) current_box.fn  = '';\n    }\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ async function set_comparand()\n  async function set_comparand(n) {\n    if (!current_box || routing_kind(current_box) !== 'comparator') return;\n    current_box.routing.comparand = n;\n    await save();\n  }\n  // }}}\n\n  // {{{ async function set_n_outputs()\n  // Iterator routing's port count. Shrinking the count means\n  // wires whose from_branch is `out_<i>` with i >= new_n no longer\n  // have a port to attach to — sever them on the source side and\n  // on each destination box's copy, same pattern as the iterator\n  // slot removal did under the legacy schema.\n  async function set_n_outputs(n) {\n    if (!current_box || routing_kind(current_box) !== 'iterator') return;\n    if (typeof n !== 'number' || n < 1 || n !== Math.floor(n)) return;\n    const old_n = current_box.routing.n_outputs || 1;\n    current_box.routing.n_outputs = n;\n    if (n < old_n) {\n      const my_id = current_box.id;\n      const orphans = new Set();\n      for (let i = n; i < old_n; i++) orphans.add('out_' + i);\n      const dst_ids = new Set();\n      (current_box.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n        if (c.from_box === my_id && orphans.has(c.from_branch)) {\n          dst_ids.add(c.to_box);\n        }\n      });\n      current_box.connections = (current_box.connections || [])\n        .filter(c => !(c.from_box === my_id && orphans.has(c.from_branch)));\n      for (const dst_id of dst_ids) {\n        const dst = Boxes.boxes[dst_id];\n        if (!dst) continue;\n        dst.connections = (dst.connections || [])\n          .filter(c => !(c.from_box === my_id && orphans.has(c.from_branch)));\n        try { await API.put_box(dst_id, dst); }\n        catch (e) { console.error('failed to clean wires to ' + dst_id + ': ' + e.message); }\n      }\n    }\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n  // }}}\n  // }}}",
          "replace_all":false,
          "old_string":"  // {{{ Iterator helpers (issue 221)\n  // Iterator boxes are pure routing primitives: input copies straight\n  // to one output, the dispatch layer (phase 3, issue 304) advances a\n  // counter mod #iterator_outputs each call. No ref/fn — the box body\n  // is just the counter + slot list. Each slot has a user-renamable\n  // name; the slot name lands in a connection's `from_branch` field\n  // exactly like a comparator branch name.\n  //\n  // The inspector edits the slot list; the dispatch layer is what\n  // actually rotates between them at runtime.\n\n  function is_iterator(box) {\n    return Array.isArray(box && box.iterator_outputs);\n  }\n\n  // Toggle the box ON as an iterator. Ref/fn/comparand are mutually\n  // exclusive with iterator routing (a routing primitive has no\n  // function to invoke), so they are stripped. All outgoing wires are\n  // dropped because the output shape changes from a single dot (or\n  // lt/eq/gt) to N named slots — same shape-change-clears-wires rule\n  // as the variadic input toggle.\n  async function make_iterator() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n\n    await sever_output_wires();\n\n    delete current_box.ref;\n    delete current_box.fn;\n    delete current_box.comparand;\n    delete current_box.has_output;\n    current_box.iterator_outputs = ['output_0'];\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Toggle iterator OFF. Drop the iterator_outputs field; sever\n  // outgoing wires (their from_branch values referenced slot names\n  // that no longer exist). The user re-picks a function via the\n  // browse button to restore ref/fn.\n  async function unmake_iterator() {\n    if (!current_box) return;\n\n    await sever_output_wires();\n    delete current_box.iterator_outputs;\n    // Restore an empty ref/fn so the schema (which requires ref on\n    // non-iterator call boxes) accepts the save. The user picks a\n    // function via the browse button to populate them.\n    if (current_box.ref === undefined) current_box.ref = '';\n    if (current_box.fn  === undefined) current_box.fn  = '';\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Append a new slot with a placeholder name (`output_N`). The user\n  // can rename it after — placeholder is just to avoid prompting on\n  // every grow. Mirrors the variadic auto-grow pattern.\n  async function add_iterator_slot() {\n    if (!current_box || !is_iterator(current_box)) return;\n    const slots = current_box.iterator_outputs;\n    let n = slots.length;\n    // pick the lowest free `output_N` so renaming + adding doesn't\n    // collide with an existing user-named slot\n    while (slots.includes('output_' + n)) n++;\n    slots.push('output_' + n);\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Remove the slot at index `idx`. Outgoing wires whose from_branch\n  // matched the removed slot get severed; remaining slots keep their\n  // names (no rename — slot names are user-defined and free-form, no\n  // need to compact like the variadic numeric indexes).\n  async function remove_iterator_slot(idx) {\n    if (!current_box || !is_iterator(current_box)) return;\n    const slots = current_box.iterator_outputs;\n    if (idx < 0 || idx >= slots.length) return;\n    // Removing the last remaining slot collapses the iterator entirely\n    // — the user shouldn't have to know there's a separate \"toggle off\"\n    // button when the visual outcome of \"× the last slot\" is the same.\n    if (slots.length <= 1) {\n      return unmake_iterator();\n    }\n    const removed = slots[idx];\n\n    // Sever every outgoing wire on this branch.\n    const my_id = current_box.id;\n    const dst_ids = new Set();\n    (current_box.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n      if (c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed) dst_ids.add(c.to_box);\n    });\n    current_box.connections = (current_box.connections || [])\n      .filter(c => !(c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed));\n    for (const dst_id of dst_ids) {\n      const dst = Boxes.boxes[dst_id];\n      if (!dst) continue;\n      dst.connections = (dst.connections || [])\n        .filter(c => !(c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === removed));\n      try { await API.put_box(dst_id, dst); }\n      catch (e) { console.error('failed to clean wires to ' + dst_id + ': ' + e.message); }\n    }\n\n    slots.splice(idx, 1);\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n    show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n  }\n\n  // Rename slot at index `idx` to `new_name`. Renames the slot itself\n  // and rewrites `from_branch` on every outgoing wire that used the\n  // old name (both the source-box record and the destination-box\n  // copy). No-op if the name is unchanged or already taken.\n  async function rename_iterator_slot(idx, new_name) {\n    if (!current_box || !is_iterator(current_box)) return;\n    const slots = current_box.iterator_outputs;\n    if (idx < 0 || idx >= slots.length) return;\n    const old_name = slots[idx];\n    if (old_name === new_name) return;\n    if (!new_name) {\n      status_msg('slot name cannot be empty', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n    if (slots.includes(new_name)) {\n      status_msg('slot name already in use', 'error');\n      return;\n    }\n\n    slots[idx] = new_name;\n\n    const my_id = current_box.id;\n    const dst_ids = new Set();\n    (current_box.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n      if (c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === old_name) {\n        c.from_branch = new_name;\n        dst_ids.add(c.to_box);\n      }\n    });\n    for (const dst_id of dst_ids) {\n      const dst = Boxes.boxes[dst_id];\n      if (!dst) continue;\n      (dst.connections || []).forEach(c => {\n        if (c.from_box === my_id && c.from_branch === old_name) {\n          c.from_branch = new_name;\n        }\n      });\n      try { await API.put_box(dst_id, dst); }\n      catch (e) { console.error('failed to rename wires on ' + dst_id + ': ' + e.message); }\n    }\n\n    await save();\n    Canvas.mark_dirty();\n  }\n\n  // Auto-grow check used by the wire-connect path. If `from_branch` is\n  // the LAST slot of an iterator box, append a new placeholder slot\n  // and persist. Idempotent — calling again on the same slot is a\n  // no-op once a newer slot exists below it. Mirrors the variadic\n  // input auto-grow.\n  async function auto_grow_iterator_after_connect(box, from_branch) {\n    if (!is_iterator(box)) return;\n    const slots = box.iterator_outputs;\n    if (slots[slots.length - 1] !== from_branch) return;\n\n    let n = slots.length;\n    while (slots.includes('output_' + n)) n++;\n    slots.push('output_' + n);\n    try {\n      await API.put_box(box.id, box);\n      Canvas.mark_dirty();\n      if (current_box && current_box.id === box.id) {\n        show(current_box, on_change_cb, on_delete_cb);\n      }\n    } catch (e) {\n      slots.pop();\n      status_msg('iterator auto-grow failed: ' + e.message, 'error');\n    }\n  }\n  // }}}",
          "file_path":"/mnt/mtwo/programs/sora/soramech/assets/js/004-inspector.js"
        }
      }],

{
  "userType":"external",
  "parentUuid":"5946415b-daae-4f46-a0bc-7b58c219da98",
  "timestamp":"2026-05-20T21:36:59.049Z",
